requirements.quote: Packets sent on the old path MUST NOT contribute to congestion control or RTT estimation for the new path.
requirements.condition: When packets were sent on an old path and congestion control or RTT estimation is performed for a new path.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using packets sent on the old path as input to congestion control or RTT estimation for the new path.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can send packets over an old path, migrate to a new path, and verify that the new path's congestion-control and RTT state is not derived from those packets.

requirements.quote: On confirming a peer's ownership of its new address, an endpoint MUST immediately reset the congestion controller and round-trip time estimator for the new path to initial values (see Appendices A.3 and B.3 of [QUIC-RECOVERY]) unless the only change in the peer's address is its port number.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint confirms the peer's ownership of a new address and the address change is not limited to the port number.
requirements.required_behavior: Immediately reset the congestion controller for the new path to its initial values.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retaining the previous congestion-controller state after confirmation when the address change is not port-only.
requirements.why_checkable: A migration test can confirm ownership of a non-port-only new address and inspect whether the new path's congestion controller is reset immediately.

requirements.quote: On confirming a peer's ownership of its new address, an endpoint MUST immediately reset the congestion controller and round-trip time estimator for the new path to initial values (see Appendices A.3 and B.3 of [QUIC-RECOVERY]) unless the only change in the peer's address is its port number.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint confirms the peer's ownership of a new address and the address change is not limited to the port number.
requirements.required_behavior: Immediately reset the round-trip time estimator for the new path to its initial values.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retaining the previous round-trip estimate after confirmation when the address change is not port-only.
requirements.why_checkable: A migration test can confirm ownership of a non-port-only new address and inspect whether the new path's RTT estimator is reset immediately.

requirements.quote: Because port-only changes are commonly the result of NAT rebinding or other middlebox activity, the endpoint MAY instead retain its congestion control state and round-trip estimate in those cases instead of reverting to initial values.
requirements.condition: When the only change in the peer's address is its port number.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to retain its congestion-control state and round-trip estimate instead of resetting them to initial values.
requirements.why_checkable: A port-only migration test can verify that retaining both prior values is an allowed implementation behavior and is not rejected as noncompliant.

requirements.quote: A receiver of packets on multiple paths will still send ACK frames covering all received packets.
requirements.condition: When a receiver receives packets over multiple paths during migration.
requirements.required_behavior: Send ACK frames whose coverage includes all received packets across those paths.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omitting received packets from ACK coverage solely because they arrived over a different path.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver packets over multiple paths and inspect emitted ACK ranges to verify that every received packet is covered.

requirements.quote: This timer SHOULD be set as described in Section 6.2.1 of [QUIC-RECOVERY] and MUST NOT be more aggressive.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint uses a separate timer for a PATH_CHALLENGE awaiting its corresponding PATH_RESPONSE.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the timer according to Section 6.2.1 of QUIC-RECOVERY unless a justified exception applies.
requirements.why_checkable: The timer's configured duration and scheduling policy can be compared with the algorithm referenced by the requirement.

requirements.quote: This timer SHOULD be set as described in Section 6.2.1 of [QUIC-RECOVERY] and MUST NOT be more aggressive.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint uses a separate timer for a PATH_CHALLENGE awaiting its corresponding PATH_RESPONSE.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Configuring or firing the PATH_CHALLENGE timer more aggressively than the timing described in Section 6.2.1 of QUIC-RECOVERY.
requirements.why_checkable: Runtime timestamps for PATH_CHALLENGE retransmissions can be compared with the referenced recovery timing to detect an impermissibly aggressive timer.
